currentContext.business: Greaves Cotton Limited manufactures diesel, gasoline, petrol and CNG engines, pump sets, gensets, farm equipment and industrial engines, delivering precision powertrain and power solutions for automotive, agriculture, marine, construction and railway customers. currentContext.strengths: Leadership in India's diesel three-wheeler segment with domestic market share improved to ~60% (Source: Vahaan sewa)|Fuel-agnostic powertrain strategy (diesel, CNG, petrol, hydrogen concepts) enabling competitiveness across urban and rural/cargo segments|165+ year engineering legacy and manufacturing/validation capability underpinning international partnerships (e.g. Ligier for Euro V+ compliant microcar engines in Europe)|Wide distribution and service network: 200+ distributors, 20,000+ mechanics and 7,000+ retailers supporting the aftermarket business|Shift toward high-margin recurring revenue (spares, AMCs, service contracts) in Energy Solutions reducing cyclicality|Full OBD-IIB certification across diesel & CNG powertrain lineup (effective April 1, 2025) supporting regulatory compliance ahead of customer launches
currentContext.strategies: Under the GREAVES.NEXT strategic framework, the Company has sharpened its focus across five key business areas: Energy Solutions, Mobility Solutions, Industrial Solutions (IS), NBFC, and Technologies.|Continued commitment to nation-building by contributing to the Government of India's 'Make in India' initiative through developing and manufacturing world-class products domestically.|Strengthened its material subsidiary Excel Controlinkage Private Limited by acquiring an additional 10% stake (raising holding to 80%), consistent with definitive agreements signed in 2023.|Scaling the NBFC investee business (Greaves Finance Limited) via additional equity investment to support its digital-first, EV-focused lending platform.|The Company maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (published on its website) governing dividend payout determinations. Its Related Party Transactions Policy was reviewed and amended by the Board on 23rd January 2025, on the Audit Committee's recommendation, to align with the SEBI (LODR) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2024.
currentContext.expansion: Greaves has allocated significant capital expenditure over the next 5-6 years for new technology development in the Auto Engines business, aimed at enhancing capabilities and meeting upcoming regulatory requirements, with growth targeted through organic expansion, contract manufacturing and deeper international market penetration. On the ESG/infrastructure side, the Company commissioned a 700 KW solar power plant at the Industrial Engines Unit, Chikalthana, Sambhajinagar, expected to generate approximately 10,02,400 units of electricity annually. Corporate-level expansion during the year included the Company increasing its stake in material subsidiary Excel Controlinkage Private Limited from 70% to 80% (12th August 2025, per definitive agreements dated 6th April 2023), and an additional equity investment of approximately Rs 22 crore in Greaves Finance Limited (GFL) completed via a rights issue on 18th September 2025 to scale its EV-focused NBFC lending platform. At the industry level, management cites data centre capacity additions targeting 3-6 GW by FY 2029-30 as a demand driver for the Energy Solutions (genset/HHP) business, though this is an industry estimate rather than a disclosed Company project.
currentContext.mdna: Indian diesel generator market grew from $1.66 billion in FY25 to $1.83 billion in FY26, and is expected to expand at a CAGR of 7.18% over the next five years, reflecting sustained demand for reliable on-site power generation even as the national grid deficit narrows.|Growth is underpinned by continued reliance on gensets in Tier II and Tier III cities, the industrial segment, data centre and telecom demand, and infrastructure/construction-sector activity that runs ahead of formal grid-connection timelines.|By end user, the industrial segment holds a 49.02% share (process industries, warehouses, fabrication units that cannot tolerate unscheduled downtime); the commercial segment (hotels, retail chains, diagnostic labs) is upgrading to CPCB IV+ compliant models with 24/7 service contracts.|Persistent power outage frequency in Tier II/III cities (households facing 2-4 hour daily outages despite the low national deficit) continues to drive genset demand.|Infrastructure and real estate expansion (roads, metro, airports, industrial corridors) is creating multi-year requirements for rented 375-750 kVA generators at early-stage construction sites.|Proliferation of telecom towers in rural and semi-urban India supports diesel genset demand where grid extension remains uneconomical.|Adoption of rooftop solar plus battery energy storage and diesel-supply seasonality are moderating growth, though not yet displacing diesel as the primary solution for multi-hour autonomy and prime-power niches.|India's power sector had near-475 GW capacity with the national demand-supply deficit below 1%, shifting demand emphasis toward backup and standby power systems that ensure reliability.|Macro tailwinds cited: India GDP growth projected 6.8-7.2% for FY27, public capital expenditure of Rs 12.2 lakh crore per the Union Budget 2026-27, and rising data centre/digital infrastructure investment.

risks.note: Industry-wide shift toward cleaner fuels, electric mobility and emerging technologies (alternate fuels, battery storage, hybrid/gas-based solutions, software-led systems) could reduce demand for the Company's conventional (diesel/petrol/CNG) product lines.

Demand is linked to macroeconomic conditions, customer capex cycles and infrastructure activity; delays in industrial/infrastructure capex, regulatory-led transitions, or demand normalisation in certain segments may impact volumes.
Operates in competitive markets across businesses; pricing pressure, low-cost offerings and margin expectations in contracts may impact profitability and market position.

Businesses are subject to evolving regulatory requirements including emission norms, fuel policies, EV incentive structures and product compliance standards; policy changes on diesel usage, alternate fuels or emission standards could affect demand and cost structures.
Geopolitical tensions, inflationary pressures, interest rate movements, currency fluctuations and global trade uncertainties may affect demand, export performance and supply chain stability.

risks.risk: Supply chain and input cost risk
risks.note: Exposure to commodity price volatility, energy/fuel cost fluctuations and supply chain disruptions from geopolitical developments and trade barriers; dependence on certain imported components poses risk until localisation improves.
Rapid advancements across electric powertrains, components and engineering technologies require continuous investment in R&D, talent and capabilities to remain competitive.
Export-oriented businesses are subject to international standards and certification requirements; regulatory changes or non-compliance could impact market access and operations.

one-line thesis: Greaves Cotton delivered record consolidated revenue of INR 3,437cr (18% YoY) and EBITDA of INR 239cr (76% YoY) driven by disciplined core business execution, with Energy Solutions growing 20% and Mobility Solutions 16%, while EV unit losses halved and international revenue rose to 13% of total — what matters is the structural margin expansion in core businesses and the path to profitability in EVs through scale and product innovation.
financial scorecard: revenue: +18% YoY (consol: INR 3,437cr); EBITDA/margin: +76% YoY (consol: INR 239cr, 7% margin); PAT (rptd): INR 154cr PBT before exceptional items; PAT (normalized): INR 170cr (ex-INR 16cr ePowertrain impairment); order book: INR 35cr single largest genset order (end-to-end); net debt: Healthy cash balance, no net debt mentioned, CAPEX disciplined
guidance: revenue growth: 16-18% YoY for core businesses; margin: 13-15% EBITDA margin target for core; order inflow: Targeting international expansion in Europe/Middle East; capex/commissioning: INR 500-700cr over 5 years, focused on R&D, automation, and global footprint
order book & pipeline: INR 35cr end-to-end genset order (supply, installation, commissioning, maintenance); defense engine order executing; L5 EV orders in advanced discussions
segment / subsidiary detail: Energy Solutions: 20% YoY growth, 35% aftermarket growth, 650kVA in-house engine launched; Mobility Solutions: 16% YoY growth, 63% market share in diesel 3-wheelers, Euro V+ exports to Ligier (Europe); Industrial Solutions: 15% YoY growth, defense and agri OEM wins; Excel Controlinkage: Double-digit domestic growth, export recovery underway, 100% acquisition planned in Q2FY27
growth verticals / optionality: Entry into 1000kVA+ gensets for data centers; low-speed EV segment (Reo brand already active); defense and marine engine expansion; European EV market penetration via Ampere brand
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expansion in core driven by cost optimization, automation, and mix shift; near-term pressure from aluminum/copper/platinum commodity inflation, partially offset by Q1 price passthrough and operating leverage
capex / expansion: INR 500-700cr over 5 years; allocated to: 1) Product development (new gensets, EV motors), 2) Operational capability (automation, AI inspection, conveyor lines), 3) International expansion (Europe, Middle East); FY26 actual CAPEX: INR 30-36cr
capital allocation: Prioritizing core business CAPEX, disciplined R&D in EV and energy tech, 100% acquisition of Excel in Q2FY27, no dividend policy mentioned, EV business funded via parent support until profitability
risks & watch-items: Commodity price volatility, EV market competition and funding constraints, geopolitical disruption in exports, delayed IPO timing due to market volatility, integration risks from new product launches
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, execution-focused; strong emphasis on profitability over volume in core, transparent on EV losses, optimistic on international and tech innovation, cautious on macro
non-obvious takeaways: 1) 650kVA genset is fully in-house engine — rare in Indian genset market; 2) Rare-earth-free EV motors piloted — potential cost and supply chain advantage; 3) 350 new retailers onboarded with 3,000 target by FY27 — retail network scaling is a hidden margin lever; 4) Defense engine repowering trucks — strategic entry into defense supply chain

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.
